$comment: §28 and §29. Capability and permitted retention are two different questions.

permitted_retention.why_not: §28. No construct is chosen, so nothing establishes that a body is needed at all. Retaining one because the transport can is capability deciding policy.

why_this_is_not_a_side_policy.$comment: The finding that connects §28 to the governance verdict.
why_this_is_not_a_side_policy.claim: what is retained decides which governance regime the act falls under. Retaining response bodies retains the publisher's content, which is squarely the reuse-of-content question source-registry-v1.md §1 rule 8 governs. Retaining a status line and named headers is closer to a record of our own request and its transport outcome.
why_this_is_not_a_side_policy.and_the_bound_on_that_claim: this is a DISTINCTION, not a legal conclusion. §50 forbids calling either side permitted, and nothing here asserts that a header-only capture escapes any obligation. What it establishes is that the two are different acts and that choosing between them is a governance decision rather than an implementation detail.

existing_retention_policy_applicability.governs: records acquired from a REGISTERED source
existing_retention_policy_applicability.why: the targets would not be registered sources, so which retention baseline applies is part of the same unanswered governance question as GOV-1 and GOV-3.
